title: Santa Monica honored the legacy of Silas White with street renaming
description:
Santa Monica honored the legacy of Silas White with the renaming of a portion of Vicente Terrace to Silas White Street.

White was a prominent Black entrepreneur in Santa Monica in the 1950’s who envisioned creating the Ebony Beach Club, a space where Black families could gather and enjoy the beach.

The ceremony marked an important step in the city’s ongoing restorative justice work, acknowledging our history and honoring those who helped shape our community.

The renaming follows Santa Monica City Council’s settlement agreement with the White family and the establishment of Oct. 12 as Silas White Day in Santa Monica.
transcript_text: Silas White >> We just are so excited that so many people have come out today as we get ready to rename [music] this portion of San Vicente Terrace as Silas White Street. >> It's so important to come out today [music] and pay tribute to Silas White with this street naming because of the [music] fact that he was one of the shapers of the African-American community around leisure in the 1950s. [music] He having this beach club here, the Ebony Beach Club. >> Silas White's [music] daughter, Connie, you have inspired us. We are establishing a $5.5 billion restorative justice fund because we [music] want a community center process to tell us what does restoring or repairing past harms look like. Thank you for trusting us on the [music] process. Thank you to your attorney for working with us. >> We have made another step forward as far as restorative [music] justice goes in doing the street naming for Silas White. Again, this is a wonderful day [music] in Santa Monica history and it's a wonderful day in black Santa Monica history because it shows that we can look at the past and grow from the past and reimagine [music] a more inclusive future.
